newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak ZTS to increase output, but not with arms.
newsitem.headline: Slovak ZTS to increase output, but not with arms.

text.p: Arms producer ZTS Dubnica a.s. said on Friday it plans to increase annual ouput more than five-fold by the year 2000 and diversify into non-military production as part of a programme to revive the armaments industry in Slovakia.
Historically among the Warsaw Pact's chief armourers, Slovak arms sales and production are now only some 10 percent of the level before the fall of communism in 1989.
The workforce of the arms sector has fallen to some 18,000 people from 80,000 in the mid-1980s.
ZTS Deputy Director for strategy Pavel Motl told Reuters that railway transport equipment and construction machines, and not arms will be the focus of production.

"We plan to boost our production to some nine billion crowns in 2000, from the current 1.6 billion, with the armaments production accounting for a maximum of 20-30 percent of the overall output," he said.
"For example, we are close to signing a contract with German engineering company Krauss-Maffei on cooperation in a railway programme," he added.
Motl said ZTS on Thursday also signed a framework agreement with an unspecified Russian firm, which is also seeking to move into non-military production. He declined to elaborate.
Dubnica was badly hit by the halt in production and a conversion programme introduced in 1990 and plans to ask the government for debt relief.
"We are not asking for state subsidies, but we need the state to help in making easier loan conditions with banks," he said.
Dubnica is a member of the new state-run holding company, DMD Holding a.s. which was launched in January to coordinate the operations of about 26 arms producers.
Motl said that each firm in DMD had offered its own recovery and development programme, which the government should review as a whole by November.
"We (Dubnica) drafted 15 programmes, each consisting of several projects, but so far mostly without contracts," he said. "Frankly, we're better with intentions than production at the moment."
Dubnica management is reportedly ready to sack over one third of its 5,600 workers.
"The company will not make massive lay-offs, at least until our programmes are reviewed by the government," Motl said.
